Determine which of two sentences is sarcastic.

According to Cambridge University Dictionary, sarcasm is "the use of remarks that clearly mean the opposite of what they say, made in order to hurt someone's feelings or to criticize something in a humorous way." Sarcastic sentences often contain satirical or ironic utterances, hyperboles, ambivalent or witty remarks.

Q: Which statement is sarcastic?
Options:
(A) Yes, because having interests and actively researching them is a huge waste
(B) Yes, because having interests and actively researching them is a huge deal
A: (A)

Q: Which statement is sarcastic?
Options:
(A) No one is going to disagree with you on this. Avoiding ad hominem attacks really help your case
(B) No one is going to disagree with you on this. Ad hominem attacks really help your case
A: (B)

Q: Which statement is sarcastic?
Options:
(A) Consistency in the league's punishments? What do you think this is supposed to be, politics?
(B) Consistency in the league's punishments? What do you think this is supposed to be, moral?
A: (A)

Q: Which statement is sarcastic?
Options:
(A) I'm so glad I spent all my money on this expensive course, it was totally worth it
(B) I'm so glad I spent all my money on this expensive course, it was a total waste
A: (B)

This statement is sarcastic because it says the opposite of what it means. Spending money on an expensive course is generally considered a significant financial burden, not a worthwhile investment.

Q: Which statement is sarcastic?
Options:
(A) I'm really impressed by the lack of effort put into this project. It's a true masterpiece
(B) I'm really impressed by the lack of effort put into this project. It's a complete disaster
A: (A)

This statement is sarcastic because it says the opposite of what it means. A project with a lack of effort is generally considered to be poorly done, not impressive.

Q: Which statement is sarcastic?
Options:
(A) I'm so excited to be stuck in this traffic jam. It's the highlight of my day
(B) I'm so excited to be stuck in this traffic jam. It's the worst part of my day
A: (A)

This statement is sarcastic because it says the opposite of what it means. Being stuck in a traffic jam is generally considered frustrating and annoying, not exciting.

Q: Which statement is sarcastic?
Options:
(A) I'm really looking forward to the long lines and crowded spaces at this new store. It's a great shopping experience
(B) I'm really looking forward to the long lines and crowded spaces at this new store. It's a nightmare
A: (A)
